Sasha: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of customers reporting weird token spikes when a client reconnects and the stream gets truncated mid-toolcall. Console shows provisional + confirmed tokens double-counting.
Ara: Hmm. Any repro or logs? :thinking_face:
Sasha: Repro is pretty small. Start a streaming toolcall, drop connection around the last chunk, client reconnects and resumes. Ledger shows the suffix tokens attributed to both sessions.
Sasha: Minimal repro log:
```
[router] session_start id=abc123
[worker] toolcall chunk seq=45 bytes=120
[router] conn_lost id=abc123
[router] resume start=46 session=def456
[worker] toolcall truncation eof=45
[ledger] add provisional tokens session=abc123 range=1-45
[ledger] add confirmed tokens session=def456 range=46-80
```
Mike: Is the issue the router claiming ownership of the trailing partial suffix before worker confirms EOF? We've seen heuristics like "claim-on-handoff" bite us.
Jordan: Sounds like a race: resume path creates a new session and the ledger bookkeeping treats the truncated suffix as owned by both the old provisional session and the new confirmed session.
Ara: Can you paste the resume protocol headers? Curious if session id or sequence boundaries differ.
Sasha: Here's the resume handshake excerpt (simplified):
```
POST /v1/streams/resume
Headers: Session-Id: def456; Resume-From: token-46
Body: { last_ack: 45 }
```
Eva: I think the core is the prefix/suffix capture window we use for provisional credits. If we don't tombstone the old provisional when we hand off, UI + billing both show the temporary credit until reconciliation.
InfraBot: Note: this thread triggered alert infra/ledger-sampling-2 at 2026-03-05T10:12Z
Mike: Two options: (A) make router delay provisional write until worker confirms EOF for suffix tokens (adds latency on edge) or (B) add a reconciliation flag in the ledger and surface provisional vs confirmed in the console so customers see "provisional pending".
Jordan: (B) is lower-risk but shifts complexity to billing reconciliation processes and UI explanations.
Ara: We should also consider partial-toolcall semantics: if a client explicitly reconnects/resumes, maybe we should require an idempotency token so the ledger can dedupe on resume.
Sasha: Idempotency token would help, but not all clients set it. We need a defenses-in-depth approach.
Eva: UX note — when we do (B) we should add an alert in the per-route dashboard showing provisional token % and a link to reconciliation details. That will reduce ops noise.
Mike: Also would be good to add a streaming metric: "resume_revs" with labels {route, cause=truncate|client_drop} so we can quantify how often this path triggers.
Ara: Agreement: short-term -> implement console provisional flag + dashboard annotation; medium-term -> router change to prefer confirmed EOF claims; long-term -> require/encourage idempotency token in SDK and validate in gateway.
Sasha: I'll open an RFC for the router change and include performance simulation numbers for added latency. I'll also add a small repro harness so SRE can stress-test.
Jordan: I'll mock up a dashboard tile and a console banner for provisional tokens. Ping me when the API for reconciliation flags is ready.
Eva: I'll update the runbook to include a troubleshooting checklist: how to find orphaned provisional sessions and force-reconcile if needed.
Sasha: Thanks all. Quick follow-ups: @Mike can you add the new metric stub to the ingestion proto? @Ara can you file the ledger migration tickets? I'll start the RFC.
Mike: On it, will send a PR for the proto today.
Ara: Filing tickets now.
InfraBot: CI job queued: tests/stream-resume-harness on infra-ci-3
Sasha: Great — let's sync tomorrow 11am PT for a short design walkthrough. :thumbsup:
